newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-KORDA WINS, THEN QUITS CZECH DAVIS CUP TEAM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KORDA WINS, THEN QUITS CZECH DAVIS CUP TEAM.

text.p: Veteran Petr Korda brought fifth-seeded Czech Republic back from the brink of elimination, beating India's Leander Paes to level their Davis Cup World Group first round tie.

Korda, who announced after the match he was retiring from Davis Cup play, won a hard fought 5-7 6-3 6-4 6-1 over Indian number one Paes in the first reverse singles on Sunday, setting a showdown between Czech number two Jiri Novak and Mahesh Bhupathi.
Korda, ranked 33rd in the world, had little trouble in dispatching Paes, overpowering the Indian with steady play at the net and powerful groundstrokes from the baseline.
Korda squandered five break points in the first set, while Paes, ranked 105 in the world, took advantage of the only one he had to take the first set in 53 minutes.
But Korda showed no signs of a cold that has plagued him throughout the week, quickly getting back on track to take the next three sets.

After the win, Korda said he would no longer play for the Czechs in the Davis Cup, complaining of the demands it put on a player. "There was a lot of pressure on me for this match, but I showed the kind of player I am," he said.
"I have thought about retiring (from Davis Cup) for a while and it's time to leave. It is a very tiring, draining experience and I think you should leave at the top. Now is the right time," he said.
Korda, who once ranked as high as fifth in the world, has been the anchor of the Czech team since his debut in 1988, compiling a 30-12 overall record, including three wins against India this weekend.
